review.summary: The three recordings are complete, but too few satellites were tracked cleanly to measure the sensor's height precisely, so no steadiness result is reported.
findings: Raw logs are complete and decode to RINEX (7156, 7200 and 7200 one-second epochs; GPS, GLONASS, Galileo and BeiDou; L1 and L5). Nothing is corrupted.
NOAA NETP posted no data after 2026-11-14 19:00 UTC, so sessions 2 and 3 have no NETP overlap; all three were processed against ZHU1 (19 km), which shares only L1 with this receiver.

Satellites in the north-east half of the sky (azimuth 0-135 deg), including some near the zenith, arrived at 19-31 dB-Hz and lost carrier lock in 36-94% of one-second steps (L1-L5 geometry-free check, not only the receiver's lock flags). Satellites to the south and west arrived at 37-50 dB-Hz and tracked cleanly.

A median of 7, 11 and 12 satellites (sessions 1-3) were held without a phase break for 10 minutes or more, all to the south and west, so height cannot be separated from horizontal position and clock error (scripts/groundtruth_diagnostics.py).

No processing gave an ambiguity-fixed solution. Relative GPS (NETP, ZHU1) and multi-GNSS float PPP (CNES real-time orbits, clocks and biases) gave session heights that move by 0.5-5 m with reasonable processing choices, and no solution settled within a session.
The receiver output MSM4, which carries no Doppler, so cycle slips cannot be repaired from Doppler.
review.not_reported: No session-to-session height scatter is reported, because any number would depend on processing choices rather than on the sensor.

rough_heights_by_method.note: Final session heights from each processing method, in metres relative to that method's own average. Exploratory runs on 2026-11-15; none is ambiguity-fixed and none is a result. With usable data every row would agree to within millimetres.
